data.body_html:
A sunset photoshoot on a yacht in Marbella is one of the most iconic ways to capture the Costa del Sol's golden hour. With the Sierra Blanca mountains behind you and the Mediterranean turning liquid gold, the light from 20:50 to 21:45 (June–August 2037) is unmatched. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, offering direct access to calm waters and stunning backdrops. Whether you're planning a couple's shoot, a fashion editorial, or a social media campaign, this guide covers everything from boat selection to golden hour timing. All charters include a licensed skipper, drinks, snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA – no hidden extras. Ready to book? Explore our full fleet and reserve your slot.

Why a sunset yacht photoshoot in Marbella works

Marbella's position on the southern coast gives you long, warm sunsets even in peak summer. The golden hour light here is soft and diffused, avoiding harsh shadows common in midday shoots. From the deck of a yacht, you get 360-degree views – the coastline, the sea, and the sky – all in one frame. The calm waters of the Alboran Sea also create mirror-like reflections, especially in the 30 minutes before sunset. For a photoshoot, this means you can shoot from multiple angles without moving locations. The temperature drops to a pleasant 24–28°C, making it comfortable for models and photographers alike.

Best yachts for a sunset photoshoot in Marbella

Choosing the right boat depends on your group size and the aesthetic you want. For intimate shoots (up to 5 people), the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) offer open decks and minimal obstructions – ideal for clean, minimalist shots. For larger groups (up to 12 pax), the Mangusta 80 (24m) provides a spacious flybridge, sleek lines, and a free jet ski for water-level action shots. The Ferretti 94 (29m) is the ultimate luxury backdrop with its expansive sundeck and elegant profile. For a cost-effective 2-hour session, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) at €749/2h or the Azimut 39 (12.5m) at the same rate are excellent choices – both include drinks, snacks, and a skipper.

Golden hour timing in Marbella 2037

Sunset times vary significantly by month. In June 2037, sunset is around 21:45, with golden hour from 20:50 to 21:45. By August, sunset shifts to 21:15, so golden hour runs 20:30–21:15. In spring (April), sunset is around 20:30, golden hour 19:45–20:30. Autumn (October) sees sunset at 19:30, golden hour 18:45–19:30. We recommend booking a 2-hour charter starting 30 minutes before golden hour, giving you time to cruise to the best spot and set up. For a full sunset-to-dusk shoot, the 4-hour option on a Tier B boat (€4,719) includes a jet ski and ample time for multiple setups.

What's included in your sunset photoshoot charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no additional fees for photographers or videographers. For Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 and Mangusta 80 Grey), a jet ski is included free – perfect for capturing dynamic shots from the water. All yachts depart from Puerto Banús, with parking available nearby. We recommend bringing your own camera gear, but the skipper can assist with positioning the boat for optimal light. For pricing on other boats (e.g., Ferretti 94, Pershing 46), contact us via WhatsApp.

Tips for a flawless sunset photoshoot on a yacht

  • Book early: Peak sunset slots in July and August fill up 2–3 weeks in advance. Contact us via WhatsApp to secure your preferred date.
  • Dress for the light: White, cream, and pastel tones reflect golden hour light. Avoid black or busy prints that absorb light and distract.
  • Bring a reflector: A small collapsible reflector can bounce light onto faces, especially useful as the sun dips below the horizon.
  • Use the jet ski: On Tier B boats, the free jet ski allows for unique water-level shots – great for dynamic angles.
  • Plan for wind: Evenings can be breezy. Use hairspray or bring a light jacket for between shots. The boat's cabin offers shelter if needed.
  • Check the moon phase: A crescent moon adds a magical element to dusk shots. In 2037, new moon dates (e.g., June 23, July 23) give darker skies for starry backdrops.

Best locations for sunset photos near Puerto Banús

Within 10–15 minutes of departing Puerto Banús, you can reach several photogenic spots. Cala del Faro offers a rocky coastline with a lighthouse – ideal for silhouettes. Cala Cortés is a quiet cove with turquoise water, perfect for reflection shots. For a backdrop of Marbella's Golden Mile and La Concha mountain, anchor just off the coast between Puerto Banús and the Marbella Marina. Further south, the coast near Estepona provides long, uninterrupted views of the sunset over the water. Your skipper will know the best spots based on wind and sea conditions.
